findings.issue: The listen clip starts too late. QUL's word timings give the 'لَا ٱلضّ' join to word 8, so the clip (42240 ms) begins about 0.7 s into the long ā. The student never hears the ض the prompt mentions, and only hears about three quarters of the six-count madd they are asked to name. That makes it sound much like the madd ʿāriḍ at the stop.

findings.issue: In the tap_letters passage the آ of ٱلضَّآلِّينَ is a separate, unkeyed tile. It is pronounced heavy because it follows the ض, so a careful student may tap it and lose marks. The ص/ط/غ/ض keys and the ر exclusion are correct (6 letters: صِ طَ غَ غْ ضُ ضَّ).
findings.evidence: Letter keys in new/umm.json umm-9 Q2 checked against the seven always-heavy letters (خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ) in 1:7. The 1:6 passage (umm-8 Q5) has no separate alif tile after a heavy letter, so it doesn't have this problem.

proposed.from: Tap every heavy letter in this verse. Leave out the ر: it is heavy in one word and light in another, so it is not counted here.
proposed.to: Tap every one of the always-heavy letters in this verse. Leave out the ر (it is heavy in one word and light in another) and the alif, which only follows the letter before it.

findings.issue: The correct option for istiṭālah ('using the tongue to fill the mouth') follows the video's loose wording, but filling the mouth describes heaviness (tafkhīm/iṭbāq) more than istiṭālah. The standard definition is the sound stretching along the side of the tongue, from back to front. The lead may want the option to carry both.
findings.evidence: Standard definition of istiṭālah: the sound of the ض extends along the edge of the tongue from its beginning to its end. umm_9 transcript: 'when you use your tongue to fill your mouth producing a sound similar to this'.

proposed.from: Using the tongue to fill the mouth, so the sound stretches along it
proposed.to: The sound stretches along the side of the tongue, from the back towards the front

findings.issue: 'Come clearly from the throat' doesn't separate ع from the hamzah, which is also a throat letter (deepest part). The rubric's point is that ع turns into a hamzah, so the prompt should name where the ع is made.
findings.evidence: Makhārij: ء ه = deepest throat, ع ح = middle of the throat. The paper's own Q2 diagram uses throat_middle for ح.

proposed.from: Why must the ع in ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ come clearly from the throat? What goes wrong if it doesn't?
proposed.to: Why must the ع in ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ come clearly from the middle of the throat? What goes wrong if it doesn't?

findings.issue: Live paper; the key is correct for the hadith as the video gives it ('lā ṣalāta li-man lam yaqraʾ bi-Fātiḥat al-Kitāb', Bukhārī 756 / Muslim 394, from ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit). But the prompt is a quote with no attribution, and two distractors ('Makrūh', 'Valid if he recites another surah') are close to a real fiqh position (Ḥanafī: Fātiḥah wājib, not farḍ). Tying the prompt to the hadith keeps the key unarguable. I checked the other Umm 1 attributions and they hold: As-Sabʿ al-Mathānī in 15:87 and Bukhārī (Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Muʿallā; Abū Hurayrah); the 'two lights' in Muslim 806 (Ibn ʿAbbās); 'nothing like it in the Tawrāh, Injīl, Zabūr or Furqān' in Tirmidhī (Abū Hurayrah/Ubayy); 'a third of the Qur'an' is Al-Ikhlāṣ; Umm al-Qurā = Makkah (6:92, 42:7).

summary: The answer keys are sound. All 65 questions pass the structural checks (totals, one correct option, rubric sums, count = script instances 0). The Arabic in prompts and options matches the Uthmani text of 1:1–7 and 16:98; the only differences are shaddah/ḥarakah order and آ vs ا+madda. The diagram answers are right (ح and ع throat_middle, ه throat_deep), and the tap_letters keys for 1:6 (ص ط ق) and 1:7 (ص ط غ غ ض ض) are correct with the ر left out on purpose. Umm 1 (live) has no errors. There are two real problems in Umm 9. Q8 asks students to compare with a week-1 Fātiḥah recording that the final Ghunna 1 never asks for. Q7's listen clip starts about 0.7 s late and cuts off the ض and the start of the six-count madd. That second one is systemic: QUL word timings give the joined sound across a waṣl to the previous word, so other courses' listen clips that start on a joined word may be clipped the same way. The rest is wording (Umm 9 Q5 'allowed', istiṭālah, 'from the throat'), one ambiguous alif tile, and stale review notes in Umm 3, 4 and 8.
